events.title: Roman Emperor Valentinian III Is Assassinated
events.description: While practicing archery on the Campus Martius in Rome, Valentinian III was struck down by two retainers of Hunnic origin. They were loyal to the general Aetius, whom the emperor had killed the year before.
events.significance: His death ended the Theodosian dynasty in the West. It hastened the chaotic final two decades of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Magellan Reaches the Philippines
events.description: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition landed on the island of Homonhon. It was the first European arrival in the archipelago, during the voyage that would become the first circumnavigation of the globe.
events.significance: The landing opened the Philippines to European contact and the start of Spanish colonization. It was a key step in the first voyage around the world.

events.title: U.S. Military Academy at West Point Is Established
events.description: President Thomas Jefferson signed legislation creating the Army Corps of Engineers. It was to found and operate a military academy at West Point, New York.
events.significance: West Point became the nation's first military college. It trained generations of engineers and army leaders.

events.title: Robert Goddard Launches the First Liquid-Fueled Rocket
events.description: In a snowy field in Auburn, Massachusetts, physicist Robert Goddard launched a rocket powered by gasoline and liquid oxygen. The flight lasted only a couple of seconds.
events.significance: The brief flight proved liquid propellants could work. It laid the groundwork for modern rocketry and, eventually, spaceflight.

events.title: Hitler Announces German Rearmament
events.description: Adolf Hitler ordered Germany to rearm and reintroduce military conscription. This openly defied the military restrictions of the Treaty of Versailles.
events.significance: The move showed that Britain, France and other powers would not enforce the postwar settlement. It was a major step on the road to World War II.
